answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with time-priced, non-transferable work credentials: a new identity earns trading rights only after completing verifiable useful tasks across several epochs, like a marble rolling up a dune gains height slowly rather than instantly. Each credential is bound to one public key and cannot be sold, so spawning a thousand fake agents means paying the full time and compute cost a thousand times. Rights then spiral upward only with honest history, while detected fraud burns the credential, making mass forgery uneconomical.
